subject: Post-demo: data handling, telemetry sharing, and next steps

Subject: Post-demo: data handling, telemetry sharing, and next steps

Hi Alice — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap
- Main concerns: PII exposure in logs, retention windows for telemetry, and whether telemetry/usage is shared with marketplace/cloud partners.
- Environment: you plan to run a mix of hosted API for prototyping and dedicated pools for production traffic.

Questions we committed to clarify
1) What PII fields might be included in requests (user_id, email, free-form text) and options for masking/pseudonymization.
2) Default and configurable retention windows for request logs and aggregated telemetry.
3) Which subprocessors receive telemetry or usage data (marketplace billing, analytics vendors).
4) Marketplace flow: does enabling AWS Marketplace listing require forwarding any customer-level telemetry?

What I can share now
- We do not forward free-form request content to third-party telemetry vendors by default; we can configure prefix-only telemetry sharing or send only aggregated metrics.
- Default request-log retention for Hosted is 30 days; for Dedicated we offer configurable retention up to 24 months under contract.
- We keep a living subprocessor list (team will attach CSV) and our SOC2 summary.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
A) Rishi to respond with specifics on PII handling, marketplace flows, and attach subprocessor list + SOC2 summary (target: EOD Mon).
B) You to share FinLytics privacy checklist / procurement gating criteria.
C) Schedule a 30–45m tech deep-dive with your security lead to nail down encryption/KMS and retention SLAs.

Tentative times I can propose for the deep-dive: Tue/Wed next week 10:00–12:00 PT. If procurement needs to join, please loop them in.

Attachments we'll provide: redwood_subprocessors_2027.csv, SOC2-summary-2026.pdf (I asked Rishi to attach).

Thanks — Vivek

Hi Vivek — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we set the tech deep-dive: 

Priority items for FinLytics
- Retention: our compliance team requires logging retention of request metadata for at least 13 months. Please confirm how that is supported on Hosted vs Dedicated.
- PII: we must ensure user-identifying fields (email, user_id) are either never written to long-term logs or are pseudonymized/hashed before storage. Are there built-in request redaction hooks?
- Marketplace: if we purchase via AWS Marketplace, will any customer-level identifiers or request-level metadata be forwarded to Amazon or any marketplace clearing account? We need confirmation in writing.

I've attached our privacy matrix (FinLytics-privacy-checklist.xlsx) for your security review. Also please copy Procurement (procurement@finlytics.com) on the contract/data-sharing language we need — they will review any redlines.

We can do the technical deep-dive on Wed 10:30 PT if that works for your team. Please include whoever manages KMS/encryption.

Best,

Hi Alice — copying answers inline to help procurement/security review. Please see attachments referenced below.

PII & request handling- Default behavior: request payloads are only stored in ephemeral request logs (30 days for Hosted by default). For Dedicated customers we provide a config option to set retention windows up to 24 months in the console or via contract.
- Redaction hooks: yes — we offer request-time redaction rules you can apply server-side (regex or field-based). We also support automatic hashing/pseudonymization for configured user identifiers (e.g., user_id, email) before writing to logs.
- Pseudonymization: stored identifiers are hashed using customer-key-wrapped salts when on Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we pseudonymize using per-customer salts managed by Redwood unless you provide a customer-managed KMS key.

Telemetry & subprocessors- Marketplace flows: enabling AWS Marketplace listing requires sending aggregated usage metrics to the Marketplace billing pipeline for billing and license reconciliation only. No free-form request text or customer PII is forwarded to Amazon. Identifiers are limited to billing account IDs and anonymized instance IDs. We can provide a statement for contract inclusion.
- Third-party telemetry vendors: we do ship aggregated telemetry (event counts, latency percentiles) to selected analytics partners; we do not ship request bodies or raw user identifiers to those vendors by default.
- Subprocessor list: attached file redwood_subprocessors_2027.csv contains current subprocessors and their roles (billing, infra, telemetry, logging). Note this list is maintained and updated; we will notify customers of material changes.

Retention specifics- Request logs: Hosted default 30 days, configurable by support up to 24 months under an enterprise agreement.
- Aggregated metrics: retained at 3 years for trend analysis unless requested otherwise.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_2027.csv, SOC2-summary-2026.pdf

Next steps we suggest:
1) Rishi to share short contract language around marketplace telemetry and a statement we can include as an appendix.
2) Tech deep-dive Wed 10:30 PT — I will bring our infra/security engineer to discuss KMS options and redaction rules.
3) Procurement to share target contract dates; we can provide an MCP for retention SLAs on Dedicated.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
